searched: Google Brain founding: Google’s blog post of 26 June 2012 (Dean and Ng byline; names Quoc Le as experiment lead but not Google Brain or Greg Corrado), the Google Brain Team look-back of 12 January 2017 (Dean posting on behalf of the team; not used), Google’s author page for Dean, Dean’s Daedalus essay (2022), and university seminar pages (Johns Hopkins 2018, MIT CSAIL 2018). Jeff Dean’s Google Research profile (research.google/people/jeff/ and variants), which search results quote as saying he co-founded Google Brain in 2011, returned HTTP 404 directly and through the relay; no archive capture was retrievable, so his co-founding rests on the Johns Hopkins speaker biography (secondary). No new source tying Greg Corrado to Brain by name was found beyond the existing pack record. Labs: Reflection AI (reflection.ai home, about, blog, newsroom: no founder names; founders taken from Sequoia’s partnership announcement of 7 March 2025, an investor source; Laskin’s launch post on X could not be located); Periodic Labs (periodic.com home and launch post, Fedus’s X post of 17 March 2025, TechCrunch March and September 2025); Physical Intelligence (company homepage names no founders; Hausman’s and Finn’s own pages used; Sergey Levine’s homepage does not mention the company and the New York Times report linked from Berkeley was not retrieved, so Levine and other reported co-founders are left out); H Company (hcompany.ai home, about, team, press, newsroom; founders and the August 2024 departures from TechCrunch and Sifted, the Sifted article being paywalled beyond its first paragraph; BNN Bloomberg returned only page furniture; H’s LinkedIn statement not retrievable); Poolside (poolside.ai home, purpose, newsroom, careers); Magic (magic.dev home and blog); Imbue (imbue.com home and about). No company-stated founding date was found for Reflection, Periodic, Physical Intelligence, Poolside or Magic. Moves: Apple Newsroom (1 December 2025) for Giannandrea and Subramanya; TechCrunch (7 July 2025) for Ruoming Pang’s move to Meta (Bloomberg original paywalled; Decrypt also retrieved, not used); reports of Pang’s 2026 move to OpenAI rest on a paywalled The Information briefing and are left out; Lilian Weng’s X post of 27 July 2026 (message is an image) and TechCrunch (29 July 2026) for her departure from Thinking Machines and announced return to OpenAI, with the reason given left out as a private matter; Microsoft AI’s announcement of 6 November 2025 for the MAI Superintelligence Team. Microsoft AI’s December 2024 hires from Google DeepMind’s health team rest on Financial Times reporting not retrieved and are left out. Searches were run on 15 October 2026 with a web search tool for discovery; Wikipedia and directory pages were used only to find primary sources.
